article.title: General strike in Greece rejects militarization and austerity
article.author: Ana Vračar
article.content: A nationwide general strike in Greece drew tens of thousands onto the streets of approximately 80 towns and cities on Wednesday, November 25. Workers from both the public and private sectors protested against further austerity and war spending. “We refuse to pay with our lives and incomes for involvement in war and the profits of business groups,” the All-Workers Militant Front (PAME) stated when announcing the strike. The strike call had already been launched during the dockworkers’ international day of action against the militarization of ports at the end of October. It is expected to ripple outward in the coming weeks, including during a new national mobilization on December 15. Read more: Dockworkers at 110 ports worldwide strike against war and genocide “Today’s strike shows that the policy that is crushing our lives, that brings yet another budget of profits and war, has an adversary: the organized labor movement, the collective action of workers, of struggling farmers, of the self-employed and of the youth,” PAME wrote. The union emphasized broad participation across sectors, from construction to public transport and administration. “Through persistent organizing in the workplaces, in the face of employer intimidation, blackmail and threats, the hundreds of strike decisions taken ‘from below,’ many by unions that have taken such a decision for the first time, show that ‘the new’ and hopeful in our lives will be born out of exactly this kind of action, multiplying the sites of struggle and demand.” Workers across sectors participated in the November 25 strike. Source: PAME/Flickr The strike in Greece comes as unions across Europe continue taking action against cuts to social security made in the name of militarization. Over the past weeks, mass demonstrations and industrial actions have taken place in Italy, Spain , France , and Belgium , all demanding more investment in social protection and labor rights. “In Greece, as in Italy, inadequate wages, the rising cost of living, job insecurity and deteriorating working conditions are affecting millions of people, whilst enormous resources are being channelled into rearmament and military spending,” the Italian grassroots union Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) wrote in a statement of solidarity with PAME. “War is not a prospect for the future of the people,” echoed the Trade Union Association of Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia from the Czech Republic . “It is death, destruction, poverty, and new opportunities for profit for the arms industry, while the working class always pays the price.”
